[LFST.9.3.6] When the outbound call is persisted as a `CallIssued` atom
([RFCS.15]), replay compares the re-derived call
against the recorded atom rather than an in-memory event. The
byte-compare of [LFST.9.3.1] is **strict over every
field the recorded atom carries** — `service`, `correlation`,
`args`, `clock_ns`, `seq`, `rule_name` (the
wire-only `call_id` is absent on the recorded atom, [RFCS.15.2])
— and any difference is the effect Divergence at that `seq`. The
recomputed call and its recorded atom are diffed once.

**A `timetag` is compared as an identity, not as a value** ([RFCS.11.2]).
As the replayer compares atoms in `seq` order ([LFST.9.3.7]), it pairs each
recorded `timetag` with the re-derived atom's `timetag` the first time either
occurs, on any compare-class atom that carries one. Every later atom **must**
agree with that pairing in both directions: a recorded `timetag` met with a
second re-derived one, or a re-derived `timetag` met with a second recorded
one, is the Divergence at that `seq`. On the engine that recorded the stream,
replay re-derives the recorded values, and the pairing is the identity.
